alt.en: A worn paper title page printed in black: "New Jubilee Songs, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers of Fisk University. Collected and Harmonized by Frederick J. Work. Second Edition. Fisk University, Nashville, Tennessee. Copyrighted, June, 1902, and August, 1904." Brown stains run down its right edge.
alt.es: Portada de papel gastado impresa en negro: "New Jubilee Songs, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers of Fisk University. Collected and Harmonized by Frederick J. Work. Second Edition. Fisk University, Nashville, Tennessee. Copyrighted, June, 1902, and August, 1904." Unas manchas marrones bajan por su borde derecho.

caption.en: The title page of New Jubilee Songs, second edition (Nashville, 1904), Fisk University's songbook collected and harmonized by Frederick J. Work, which holds the earliest printing of Wade in the Water we have read.
caption.es: La portada de New Jubilee Songs, segunda edición (Nashville, 1904), el cancionero de la Universidad Fisk recopilado y armonizado por Frederick J. Work, que contiene la impresión más antigua de Wade in the Water que hemos leído.

source: Frederick J. Work, collector and harmonizer, New Jubilee Songs as Sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers of Fisk University, second edition (Nashville: Fisk University, "Copyrighted, June, 1902, and August, 1904"), title page

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "Wade in the Water", with a note in parentheses, "A favorite melody among Southern Baptists while a baptism is in progress.", and two lines of melody on single staves in 2/4 time, with one sharp, over the words "Wade in the water, Wade in the water, children, Wade in the water, God's a-going to trouble the water." The page number 8 is at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "Wade in the Water", una nota entre paréntesis, "A favorite melody among Southern Baptists while a baptism is in progress.", y dos renglones de melodía en pentagramas sueltos, en 2/4 y con un sostenido, sobre las palabras "Wade in the water, Wade in the water, children, Wade in the water, God's a-going to trouble the water." Al pie, el número de página 8.

caption.en: Page 8 of the 1904 book: the chorus of Wade in the Water printed as a bare tune on one staff, under a note calling it a favorite melody among Southern Baptists while a baptism is in progress.
caption.es: La página 8 del libro de 1904: el estribillo de Wade in the Water impreso como una melodía sola en un único pentagrama, bajo una nota que la llama melodía preferida entre los bautistas del Sur mientras se celebra un bautismo.

source: Frederick J. Work, collector and harmonizer, New Jubilee Songs as Sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers of Fisk University, second edition (Nashville: Fisk University, "Copyrighted, June, 1902, and August, 1904"), p. 8, "Wade in the Water"

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph looking through two stone arches into a vaulted chamber whose floor is still water, reflecting the stone wall beyond. A rope hangs down into the water. A strip along the bottom reads "353 Pool of Bethesda. Bethesda Teich. Piscine de Béthesda.", and "American Colony, Jerusalem" is written at the lower left.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro que mira a través de dos arcos de piedra hacia una cámara abovedada cuyo suelo es agua quieta, que refleja el muro de piedra del fondo. Una cuerda cuelga hasta el agua. Una franja en la parte inferior dice "353 Pool of Bethesda. Bethesda Teich. Piscine de Béthesda.", y abajo a la izquierda está escrito "American Colony, Jerusalem".

caption.en: A water-filled vault in Jerusalem that the American Colony's photographers labelled the Pool of Bethesda, photographed between 1898 and 1914; in John's Gospel an angel troubles the water of the pool of Bethesda, the story the chorus is read from.
caption.es: Una bóveda llena de agua en Jerusalén que los fotógrafos de la American Colony rotularon como el estanque de Betesda, fotografiada entre 1898 y 1914; en el Evangelio de Juan un ángel agita el agua del estanque de Betesda, el relato desde el que se lee el estribillo.

source: Jerusalem (El-Kouds). Pool of Bethesda (glass dry plate negative, 10 x 12 in.; caption on negative: "Pool of Bethesda"; title from the American Colony's 1914 catalogue of photographs)
library: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection
licenceEvidence: LoC catalogue record LCCN 2019698297 (https://lccn.loc.gov/2019698297/marcxml), field 540: "No known restrictions on publication."; photographer "American Colony (Jerusalem). Photo Department" (a firm, no named person); made between 1898 and 1914 (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "Wade in the Water, Concluded": two lines of melody on single staves with one sharp, with four numbered verses stacked under the notes, each line answered by "God's a-going to trouble the water".
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "Wade in the Water, Concluded": dos renglones de melodía en pentagramas sueltos con un sostenido, con cuatro estrofas numeradas apiladas bajo las notas, y cada verso respondido por "God's a-going to trouble the water".

caption.en: Page 9 of the 1904 book, where the four verses stand under the verse tune, each call answered by the same line, God's a-going to trouble the water.
caption.es: La página 9 del libro de 1904, donde las cuatro estrofas están bajo la melodía de la estrofa, y cada llamada recibe la misma respuesta, God's a-going to trouble the water (Dios va a agitar el agua).

source: Frederick J. Work, collector and harmonizer, New Jubilee Songs as Sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers of Fisk University, second edition (Nashville: Fisk University, "Copyrighted, June, 1902, and August, 1904"), p. 9, "Wade in the Water, Concluded"
